title: The King and Priest Christ
english: To limp, as Elijah says: 'How long will you limp with double inclinations?' (1 Ki 18:21). 'If he is Lord, go after him.' And perhaps everyone who has clung to the divine scripture, not meditating upon it as is necessary, is said to be limping in it, because he has not accepted it, neither walking nor limping in it.

Regarding Ps 17:47a: It is said that God lives, not by taking life but by providing it. And He himself indeed often says concerning Himself, 'I the Living am, says the Lord.' But also the Savior, saying, 'Just as the living Father sent me, and I live through the Father,' demonstrates that he lives not by a participation in life; for He himself is the life, from whom the Son, being consubstantial with the Father, is drawn. For if the Son is life, not by a sharing of life but by himself being life-giving to those who partake of him, and the Father also lives by providing life according to the same manner, the Son being given to the Father by the same energy, the same essence of the Father and Son exists. And this is what the word demonstrates: 'The Father lives,' he says, 'and I live through the Father,' as if he were saying that because of such a Father, he himself, living, exists by essence. He is the living God and is blessed, having blessed the saints with every spiritual blessing in the heavenly places (Eph 1:3). It is said that he is blessed if all blessing is in him. For everything said, thought, and spoken or thought blessedly is about him.

Regarding Ps 17:47b: 'The God of my salvation is exalted, having taken my senses to his greatness; for great are his works, and they themselves are great.' Since the salvation of the rational animal is not a small work, it is necessary that the cause of this be great. And God is exalted, not by changing from a lowly place to a high one, but by those having recognized great things concerning him.
Regarding Ps 17:50: For he confesses thanks for this progress and salvation, having taken their sins into himself, becoming an ambassador of their repentance.

For the voice 'I will confess to you' signifies both. For the Son also sings in the name of the Father, doing all things according to the will of the Father. The Father exalts the salvation of the King Christ (Ps 17:51a); it is not that the King himself is saved, but he provides [salvation] to those being saved with him. And God is the King, not as reigning of the God, but of those reclining with God. For when we say ruler of those who are ruling, we mean as a leader of them; but when we say ruler of the king, we mean according to his laws.

The voice of Christ signifies priest and king (Ps 17:51bc). If the word is about David—that is, all who are capable by hand—it shows God showing mercy to practical men, being capable in their activities, and if some of their seed happen to be from the teaching and imitation of his life; then he does mercy to these not for a passing moment or for a little while, but for an age. But if the word is about the true David regarding God ('For I will arise for you a shepherd like my servant David' [1 Sam 2:25/2 Sam 7:12]), he provides eternal mercy to him and to his seed, and his anointing and his priesthood are to be indestructible; for the old priesthood being transferred, the priesthood of Christ is inviolable.

The heavens declare the glory of God (Ps 18:2); and the glory of God is the only-begotten according to the radiance of glory, the order and the supremacy of his kingdom, according to 'And the glory of the Lord shall be seen' [Isa 60:1]. These [the heavens] declare by singing and theologizing, the powers dwelling in the heavens, named homonymously as dwelling in heavens according to the manner of metonymy. And the firmament announces the work of the active powers of God, called his hands, not only by words but by the works themselves (Ps 18:3-5b). Those who are the contemplative...
